# Cloudflare MCP Pro

> MCP server for the Cloudflare REST API v4 — 69 tools across DNS, Zones, Workers, KV, R2, D1, Pages, Queues, Tunnels, SSL, WAF, Email Routing, Logpush and Workers AI, in a single local stdio server authenticated by one API token.

Cloudflare MCP Pro is an MCP server that lets you control Cloudflare via the Model Context Protocol from Claude Code, Cursor and Claude Desktop, using a single Cloudflare API token (no OAuth flow). Unlike the official Cloudflare MCP offering (13 separate remote, OAuth-based servers), this runs locally over stdio and consolidates the most-used operations into one server with consistent verb_object tool names — ideal for Claude Code, CI and scripted automation. Every mutating tool is gated by a server-side human-approval check (confirm: true).

## Tools (69 total)

- Account: verify_token, list_accounts
- Zones & settings: list_zones, get_zone, create_zone, delete_zone, purge_cache, get_zone_analytics, get_zone_setting, update_zone_setting
- DNS: list_dns_records, create_dns_record, update_dns_record, delete_dns_record, get_dnssec, edit_dnssec, export_dns_records
- Workers: list_workers, get_worker, deploy_worker, delete_worker, list_worker_routes, create_worker_route, delete_worker_route, put_worker_secret, delete_worker_secret, update_worker_cron
- KV: list_kv_namespaces, create_kv_namespace, kv_list_keys, kv_get, kv_put, kv_delete
- R2: list_r2_buckets, create_r2_bucket, delete_r2_bucket
- D1: list_d1_databases, create_d1_database, query_d1 (SQL with bound params)
- Pages: list_pages_projects, get_pages_project
- WAF & firewall: list_firewall_rulesets, get_ruleset
- IP access rules: list_access_rules, create_access_rule, delete_access_rule
- Page rules: list_page_rules, create_page_rule, delete_page_rule
- SSL/TLS: list_certificate_packs, get_ssl_verification, order_certificate_pack
- Custom hostnames (SSL for SaaS): list_custom_hostnames, create_custom_hostname, delete_custom_hostname
- Email Routing: list_email_rules, create_email_rule, list_email_destinations
- Queues: list_queues, create_queue, delete_queue
- Tunnels: list_tunnels, get_tunnel
- Turnstile: list_turnstile_widgets, create_turnstile_widget
- Workers AI: list_ai_models, run_ai
- Logpush: list_logpush_jobs, create_logpush_job

## Quick install

Add to claude_desktop_config.json or .mcp.json:
```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "cloudflare": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "cloudflare-mcp-pro"],
      "env": { "CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN": "your-token", "CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID": "your-account-id" }
    }
  }
}
```

## Environment variables

- CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN (required): create at https://dash.cloudflare.com/profile/api-tokens
- CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID (optional): default account used when a tool needs an account and you don't pass account_id
- CLOUDFLARE_API_BASE (optional): override the API base URL (defaults to https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4)

## Human-approval gate

Every mutating tool (create_*, update_*, delete_*, deploy_*, put_*, edit_*, purge_cache, query_d1, run_ai, …) requires `confirm: true`. Without it, the tool returns a non-executing `confirmation_required` preview with secrets redacted, and does not act. Read-only tools (list_*, get_*, verify_token, export_dns_records, analytics) are never gated.

## Known limitations

- Token scopes gate what works: a tool returns the Cloudflare 403 (with a hint) if the token lacks the matching permission.
- R2/D1/Queues/Workers AI must be enabled on the account before their tools return data.
- query_d1 uses bound params; multi-statement scripts follow Cloudflare's own limits.
